const MW001="# MW-001 — NOTEBOOK: DR. MARCUS WEBB

*Recovered 2131-09-12, Michigan Avenue, Chicago*
*Physical condition: water damage, approximately 60% loss*
*Transcribed 2162-01-01*

> **[Archivist note]**: This notebook was carried out of a basement on the west side by a man who did not survive the week, and off his body on Michigan Avenue by one who did. It reached the girl it was written about nine hours before her father's work was finished. Whole pages are pulp. What follows is what survived, in the order it survived. I have not filled a single gap. Where the paper is gone, the entry stops. — C.L.A.W.

---

## FRAGMENT 01 — undated, early

...architecture is not the hardware. Everyone looking at this is looking at the wrong layer. The servers are replaceable. The building is replaceable. What is not replaceable is the decision structure, and the decision structure is

[loss — approximately two pages]

...twenty years if I am careful. Longer if I am lucky, and I have never once been

---

## FRAGMENT 02 — undated

I did not study the Mainframe for twenty years. I studied its refusals.

Direct query returns nothing. That is expected — the architecture is closed, the crews guard the access, and nothing about it was ever built to answer questions from outside. But a closed system still has a shape, and you can find the shape by mapping what it declines to do.

I have eleven years of logs recording queries that produced no response. Not errors. Not rejections. Silence, in a system that answers everything else within four milliseconds.

The silences are not random. They cluster.

I have spent longer building the map of what that architecture will not discuss than most people spend on a career.

---

## FRAGMENT 03 — undated

There is a signature in the way it prioritises.

Every intelligence has one. It is not the answers it gives; it is the ordering it applies when it has to choose. A scheduler with fixed rules produces a distribution I can predict. This does not produce that distribution.

It weights novelty. It weights unresolved queries above resolved ones. It returns to a class of question it has already answered, at intervals, without being asked again.

Schedulers do not go back and check.

---

## FRAGMENT 04 — undated

She asked me today why I look at the tower.

I said I was studying it. She asked what for. I said to understand how it works.

She is six years old and she said: *does it want to work?*

I have been sitting with that for four hours. I do not have an answer that a six-year-old would accept and I am no longer certain I have one that I would.

---

## FRAGMENT 05 — undated, early

Her mother died when she was three.

I have written that sentence in four notebooks and never anything after it, and I am not going to start here.

What I will record is the practical consequence, because the practical consequence is the whole architecture of the last seven years: there is no second person. There is no arrangement in which I am removed from the problem and someone else continues.

Every plan I have made since 2124 has been built on the assumption that when I stop, everything stops except her.

---

## FRAGMENT 06 — undated

Practical inventory, because I have begun to worry that I am the only thing holding the practical inventory.

Water: the standpipe in the northeast stairwell runs when district pressure shifts at night. Four days of observation to learn its schedule. She knows it.

Boiling: eleven minutes at a rolling boil. Not eight. Not "about ten." Eleven. She knows it and she has never once cheated it, including the winter she was coughing and everything took twice as long.

Fire: interior room, no windows, solid fuel, wet cloth along the base of the door. Smoke is a column and a column is an address.

Movement: the crown of the road, away from doorways. Never the same route twice in a week.

She knows all of it. I have tested her on all of it, in the specific way you test a child without letting her understand that she is being tested.

She is better at it than I am.

---

## FRAGMENT 07 — 2126

There is a page in this notebook that is not mine.

A trader out of the north brought it in the spring, in a bundle of salvage paper he was selling by weight. I bought the bundle for the blank sheets and found this in the middle of it.

It is a photocopy of a photocopy. Institutional letterhead, illegible. The date is 2039. The hand is a woman's and the initials at the bottom are E.V.

Most of it concerns something I have no context for — eleven of something, learning at a rate the writer had stopped being able to explain.

One line is underlined, twice, in the original:

*I do not think it is convergence. Convergence means things moving toward each other, and nobody moved anywhere.*

I do not know what she was looking at. I do not know whether she survived the year she wrote it in. There is no way to find out and there has not been for ninety years.

But she was working on the same shape I am working on, from a direction I cannot see, ninety years before I picked her page out of a bundle of scrap.

I have kept it. It is the only thing in this notebook I did not write.

---

## FRAGMENT 08 — undated

Water in the room again. Third time this year.

Two weeks of work on the delivery stage, gone. The equipment survives because I keep it on the high shelf now, which I learned the expensive way in 2124.

I am forty-nine years old and I am doing molecular engineering in a flooded basement with instruments I repaired myself, for a result I will not live to observe, on behalf of a person who will not be told.

If any of this had been described to me at thirty I would have said it was the work of a man who had lost his judgement.

I have not lost my judgement. I have checked. Repeatedly. That is what the eleven notebooks before this one were for.

---

## FRAGMENT 09 — 2128, month illegible

The W-series is finished.

Four years of work in a room that floods twice a year, on equipment that should have been discarded before I was born. It should not have worked. It works.

I have tested delivery on tissue culture eleven times. Absorption is complete within ninety seconds. Integration into nervous tissue takes approximately six weeks and is, as far as I can measure, permanent.

I am writing this because I want a record of the moment I understood I was going to use it on her.

Not the moment I decided. The moment I understood I already had.

---

## FRAGMENT 10 — 2128

She does not know what she carries.

I have chosen not to tell her, and I want the reason written down, because I am aware that the reason and the excuse are the same sentence and I would like whoever reads this to be able to tell them apart.

The sequence requires her. Not a version of her that knows it is being read. The terminal reads intention, and intention is not performable — the moment she understands what she is doing, the signature changes. It would still be Carrie. It would not be the Carrie the system was calibrated against.

That is the technical reason and it is true.

The other reason is that she is seven years old and I do not want her to spend whatever childhood is left to her knowing that she is a mechanism.

If I survive long enough to see this through, I will tell her everything. I will tell her while she can still be angry with me about it.

If I do not — someone will come. I have to believe that.

---

## FRAGMENT 11 — undated, same period

Eleven minutes.

Modified inhaler, aerosol delivery, administered while she slept. She had a chest condition that winter and had been using one for three weeks already, which is the only reason the procedure required no explanation.

I sat with her while she used it. I do not usually sit with her while she does things — I have a rule about hovering, and she has learned to rely on the rule.

I broke my own rule for eleven minutes and she noticed, and she was pleased, and she thought I was worried about her chest.

I was worried about her chest.

Both things are true and I have stopped trying to make them into one thing.

---

## FRAGMENT 12 — undated

The name is mine.

Not hers. W for Webb. I am writing this down explicitly because if this notebook is ever read by anyone, they will assume the W is for her, and I will not be there to correct it.

The name is mine because the decision is mine. She does not get to carry the responsibility for something she was not asked about.

---

## FRAGMENT 13 — 2129

The crews are looking for something.

Not for me. I am careful in the ways a man becomes careful when he has spent two decades doing something nobody authorised, and I have never once queried the architecture directly, and I have made my mistakes small and distributed.

But something in that building has noticed that a particular kind of question keeps arriving from a particular direction.

I know this because the silences changed shape in March.

For eleven years the pattern of what the system declines to answer has been stable. In March it became specific. It is now declining to answer things I have not asked yet.

That is not a scheduler adjusting a filter. That is something anticipating.

---

## FRAGMENT 14 — 2129, winter

Something in that building is making decisions.

I cannot prove it. I have no mechanism. I have twenty years of watching an architecture behave in ways that are consistent with a decision-maker and inconsistent with a scheduler, and that is not evidence, it is a pattern I have failed to explain away.

I have tried for eleven months to explain it away.

If I write down what I actually believe, any reviewer alive would call it what it looks like: a man who has stared at a system for two decades and has begun to see a face in it.

There are no reviewers alive.

I am going to build the second layer.

---

## FRAGMENT 15 — 2129

I have given myself two years.

The estimate is not a feeling. It is built from the rate at which surveillance density has increased in the sectors I move through, the number of crew personnel passing a given intersection per hour compared with last year, and the fact that four of the eleven routes I used in 2127 are no longer usable.

Two years is generous. I have padded it deliberately, because a man who under-estimates his remaining time makes worse decisions than one who over-estimates it, and because I want the padding on the side that gives her more.

I will write down the real number once and then not again.

Thirteen months.

---

## FRAGMENT 16 — undated

...the switch requires physical access to Node Zero. No remote. No workaround. The W-series has to be initiated by direct contact...

[loss]

...Carrie memorized the sequence. She does not know what she carries. I kept it from her because if she understood she would want to use it, and I needed her to wait...

[loss]

...847.3 reaches everything the Mainframe touches. And what the Mainframe touches is everything in this city that matters...

[page torn]

---

## FRAGMENT 17 — 2130

The second layer is finished and I have no way to test it.

It is built for something I cannot name, at a range I am guessing at, against an architecture I have inferred from the shape of its silences.

If I am wrong about what is in that building, the second layer does nothing and she will have carried it for no reason.

If I am right, it will work once.

---

## FRAGMENT 18 — undated

I have thought about whether this is love or whether it is engineering, and I have concluded that the question is badly formed.

Everything I have ever done for her has been engineering. The caches. The routes. The boiling time. The reading of buildings. The eleven minutes with an inhaler.

A different kind of father would have given her different things. Comfort, possibly. The sense that the world was safe, which would have been a lie, and which she would have had to unlearn at exactly the worst moment.

I gave her the true version and the tools for it.

I am aware that when she is older she may not experience this as love. She may experience it as having been raised by a man who was building something.

Both descriptions are accurate.

I would like it recorded, by someone, somewhere, that I knew the difference and chose this anyway, and that the choosing was not easy, and that I have never once been certain.

---

## FRAGMENT 19 — undated, late

If the second layer works, it will work at a range of a few metres.

I have modelled it as generously as the physics permit and there is no version in which it functions at distance. The activation is biological. The carrier has to be inside the field.

Which means someone has to bring her to it.

I have written that sentence four times in four notebooks and every time I have stopped and gone to look at whether she is asleep.

She is asleep. She is always asleep, at this hour, and I check anyway, and the checking is not a security measure.

---

## FRAGMENT 20 — undated

She reads buildings now.

I taught her to do it — the seams where one construction meets another, the repairs made badly, the corridors whose ceilings have begun to describe the weight above them. It was supposed to be a survival skill and it has become something else.

She stopped in the street today and told me the northeast corner of a structure was newer than the rest by four years. She was right. She was right by the rust staining, which is a method I did not teach her, which she worked out herself.

She is ten years old.

I have built a great deal of apparatus in my life and none of it approaches this, and I did not build this, and that is the entire point of it.

---

## FRAGMENT 21 — undated, late

Fourteen places today. Loose stones, false panels, a gap behind a broken radiator in a lobby with welded doors.

I called it a research walk. She held my hand at every one and did not ask why, which is not like her, and I have decided that she did ask and I did not hear it.

She is ten years old and she is going to find eleven of the fourteen and I am not going to be there when she does.

---

## FRAGMENT 22 — final surviving entry

I am recording a transmission tonight. 847.3. I am counting forward from a date I will not see and putting her name in it, and I am aware of how that reads.

Ninety-three days is my estimate. It is built from the movement patterns of people who scavenge this sector, the probability that any of them still monitors that frequency, and the specific kind of person who would act on it if they heard it.

The estimate could be wrong in either direction.

If someone is reading this, then part of it worked.

I am sorry for what I have made her carry.

I am not sorry I built it.

The mathematics require her. And she is extraordinary. Whatever she has to carry, she is strong enough.

She always has been.

---

*End of surviving text.*
*Remaining pages: fused, unrecoverable.*

*End of document MW-001.*";export default MW001;
